definitions.explanation: Used to describe hot weather or ambient temperature. For hot objects or drinks, use 熱い (atsui) with a different kanji.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{暑|あつ}い⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
{暑|あつ}くて⟦{眠|ねむ}れません→眠る：01181_nemuru⟧。
examples.english: It's so hot I can't sleep.
It's hot, so may I open the window?

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{去年|きょねん}→去年：00727_kyonen⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{暑|あつ}かった⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧、⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦エアコン→エアコン：05282_eakon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}いました→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: This summer was hotter than last year, so I used the air conditioner every day.

notes:
USAGE:
{暑|あつ}い describes how hot it feels — the weather, a room, the season — not the temperature of a thing you touch. It is used both before a noun ({暑|あつ}い⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧) and as a predicate (⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{暑|あつ}い). Because it describes a sensation, it takes no subject in the usual sense: {暑|あつ}い⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧ on its own means "it's hot" or "I'm hot," depending on context.

KANJI DISTINCTION:
- {暑|あつ}い (written with the "sun" radical): hot weather or air temperature
- ⟦{熱|あつ}い→熱い：09888_atsui⟧ (written with the "fire" radical): hot objects, food, or a fever

FORMS:
- Negative: {暑|あつ}くない
- Past: {暑|あつ}かった
- Adverbial: {暑|あつ}く

COLLOCATIONS:
- {暑|あつ}い⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧: hot day
- ⟦{蒸|む}し{暑|あつ}い→蒸し暑い：03751_mushiatsui⟧: humid and hot
- ⟦{暑|あつ}さ→暑さ：12973_atsusa⟧: the heat (noun form)

SIMILAR ADJECTIVES:
- ⟦{寒|さむ}い→寒い：00664_samui⟧: cold (weather) — the direct opposite
- ⟦{涼|すず}しい→涼しい：00674_suzushii⟧: cool, pleasantly so
- ⟦{熱|あつ}い→熱い：09888_atsui⟧: hot to the touch (objects, drinks, a fever)
